label: canon-c19-in12-eager-tb
_why: THE TIE-BREAKER of canon_c19_in12_eager_n2.json: the third run of the 2+1 rule, run ONLY if alignment_check.mjs reads the pair DIVERGENT (exit 2); the config is read as the median of three (pool both sessions in --arm). Same book, same predictions: THE HOARDING FIX (user, 2026-09-15 09:00 local: hoarding is a problem in itself that should be tuned by the spending-eagerness defines; a pool above a year of world GDP can spoil every measurement, and the aim is a pool BELOW vanilla's; fix it sooner rather than later). DIAGNOSIS on the C 1.9 runs (scratchpad queue_series.mjs over the save summaries): the private construction queue is a 2.0-2.4-year BACKLOG at 1935 (world 2.9-3.1M points left at 25-28k points a week) against vanilla's 0.3-0.4 years, with the private share of construction speed already 74-87% (allocation is not the limit) and the GOVERNMENT queue 2.8-3.0 years deep (vanilla 0.5) - clogged with the dear rungs the government AI builds itself (arms, artillery, motor, automotive at 1,140-4,115 points), so the construction sectors it queues take years to arrive; the pool (0.42-0.64 of GDP, Britain 0.87-2.40) is capacity-bound, not idle. Under the x1.3 lift the same shape reads 1.07 (Britain 6.97). This book keeps canon-c19-in12 (the found slope, F117) and pushes ONLY the investment-pool defines toward spending: MONEY_SPENDING_CONSTRUCTION_TOO_LARGE_INVESTMENT_POOL_FACTOR 0.9 -> 1.0 (the define's stated cap), CRITICAL_THRESHOLD 0.9 -> 1.25 and EXCESSIVE_THRESHOLD 1.5 -> 3.0 (the AI keeps rating construction very important until it holds 125% of wanted and only nice-to-have above 300%), CONSTRUCTION_MAX_NUM_PRODUCTION_BUILDING_CONSTRUCTIONS_SCALED 0.1 -> vanilla's 0.05 (fewer government-queued production buildings, so the queue carries construction sectors sooner). Not touched: PRODUCTION_BUILDING_AUTONOMOUS_INVESTMENT_WANTED_COST_COVERAGE (ruled out 2026-09-05), AUTONOMOUS_INVESTMENT_UPDATE_COUNT_DIVISOR (queueing is not the bottleneck: 2,100-2,300 items already queued), the LONG/VERY_LONG thresholds (160/240 kept). One lever (the define set) against canon-c19-in12. Full runs unless the stop rule fires: a spent hoard is more capital at work, so GDP is expected UP from 1.08x - if it passes 1.3x the slope must rise with the hoard gone (C 2.05 x1.2 + this set is the pre-registered branch).

_predictions.hoard: THE KEY PREDICTION: world pools 0.15-0.35 of a year of GDP at 1935 in both seeds (C 1.9: 0.42 / 0.64; vanilla median 0.31), Britain below 1.0 (2.40 / 0.87); the private queue backlog under 1.5 years at 1935 (2.0-2.4); construction sector levels at 1935 above 3,800 (2,971 / 3,092). Failure: pools still above 0.4 with the backlog above 2 years -> the AI cannot buy the capacity on its budget and the lever is the construction sector itself (throughput or its cost), not the AI defines.
_predictions.gdp: world GDP 1.00-1.30x the vanilla eighteen-run median at 1935 (point ~1.15x: the spent hoard is capital at work); the dip around 1900 shallower than C 1.9 (0.80-0.95x). Above 1.3x at 1936 STOPS the config and says the slope must rise with the hoard gone (branch: C 2.05 x1.2 with this set).

_predictions.obsolescence: rung 0 unchanged by this lever: 40-50% staffed at a 20-28% margin against the frontier 40%+; its level count still rising (the willingness lever is the e0ai500 batch, read separately); below-best 30-38%
_predictions.perf: row P total within +10% of vanilla median play time (more buildings under construction and standing: +0-8% expected); no crash expected, the feeder handles a mid-autosave CTD (L32)

_alignment: THE 2+1 RULE (user-ruled 2026-09-14, F114): after run 2, `node tools/testbed/ledger/alignment_check.mjs --arm <session>:canon-c19-in12-eager` - two criteria at 1935 vs the vanilla per-run median, five bands each, a pair fails an axis only in different bands AND >= 0.15 (GDP) / >= 0.10 (workers) apart. DIVERGENT => one more run of this config as its own one-run schedule (the _tb.json beside this one), the reading the median of three (pool both sessions: --arm sessA,sessB:canon-c19-in12-eager). No obsolescence criterion; rung-0 staffing / payback / below-best are verdict flags. PLUS THE RUN-LEVEL STOP (user-ruled 2026-09-14, 2+1 batches only): any run that ends above x1.3 of vanilla's 1936 GDP (the eighteen-run median at the 1936.1.1 endpoint, GBP 4,544M) is the config's LAST run - be it run 1, 2 or 3 - enforced between runs by tools/testbed/stop_watch.ps1 (drops tools/testbed/STOP after the offending run's 1936 summary lands; the next run is an 1836 stub, L17-excluded). Never mid-run. PLUS THE CAPITAL-ABUNDANCE FLAG (user-ruled 2026-09-15): `node tools/testbed/ledger/capital_flags.mjs --arm <session[,session]>:canon-c19-in12-eager` - a shortlist member (GBR, USA, FRA, GER) under 3% total unemployment INCLUDING peasants with a hoard over 2 GDP trips it; the pooled shortlist tripping is a VOID (exit 4).
